content.title: 1-seed UConn ends 6-seed Notre Dame women's basketball season in Elite 8
content.text: 1-seed UConn ends 6-seed Notre Dame women's basketball season in Elite 81 / 15A look at Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo: Photo gallery, best imagesFORT WORTH, TEXAS - MARCH 29: Hannah Hidalgo #3 of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish warms up prior to the game against the UConn Huskies at Dickies Arena on March 29, 2026 in Fort Worth, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images)FORT WORTH, Texas – Notre Dame women’s basketball’s hot streak finally fizzled when the 6-seed Irish ran into the undefeated, defending national champion 1-seed UConn in the NCAA Tournament Elite Eight Sunday, March 29 at Dickies Arena. Notre Dame’s unanimous USA Today Sports First Team All-American junior Hannah Hidalgo’s 22-point, 11-rebound double-double wasn’t enough, as the Huskies advanced to their 25th Final Four with a 70-52 win.Nearly leading UConn off the bench was Big East Conference Freshman and Sixth Player of the Year Blanca Quinonez with 20 points, while Naismith Women’s College Player of the Year finalist sophomore Sarah Strong had 21.AdvertisementMore: Notre Dame vs UConn women's basketball Elite 8 live updatesHow it happenedThe Irish got the first bucket of the game, a layup from senior Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) Most Improved Player Cassandre Prosper. In fact, Notre Dame led twice in the first quarter, but the Irish were only able to stay in front for a total of 70 seconds.UConn only led by as many as 10 in the first half, holding a seven-point advantage at halftime, but its advantage grew to as many as 14 points in the third period. However, when it was just an eight-point game with 4:43 left in the quarter, head coach Niele Ivey turned to her coaching staff and said, ‘We’re really right there.’AdvertisementAn and-one layup from senior Naismith Women’s College Player of the Year finalist Azzi Fudd gave the Huskies their new largest lead of the game at 60-42 after she converted the free throw with 6:10 left in the fourth quarter. Fudd finished with 13 points.Notre Dame grad student Iyana Moore fired back with a mid-range jumper, but Quinonez punched right back with a 3-pointer to give UConn a 19-point lead. Moore answered with another mid-range jumper, although the Irish still trailed 63-46 with 5:23 left to play.More: Hannah Hidalgo scoring, stats in Notre Dame vs UConn: Live updatesProsper fouled out with 4:23 left in the game, ending her season early. Undecided about her future, it may have been the senior’s last collegiate game. She has one more year of eligibility.AdvertisementAt that point, Notre Dame was down 63-48, and simply put, depth was UConn’s biggest advantage Sunday. The Huskies not only got 20 points from Quinonez, but they scored 32 points off the bench compared to Notre Dame’s seven.Nine players saw the floor for UConn compared to the Irish’s seven, and all nine scored. The Irish also struggled to take care of the ball, turning it over 18 times, which led to 19 Husky points.Notre Dame’s greatest strength all season was its defense, with Hidalgo leading the country in steals per game and setting an NCAA single-season steals record, but she only had three swipes against UConn.Hidalgo finished her historic season as Notre Dame's single-season scoring and steals leader, among many other records set. The Irish made the Elite Eight for the first time since 2019 behind her efforts.AdvertisementKyle Smedley is a sports reporter at the South Bend Tribune.
